narratives.name: Partner Relationship Journey
narratives.description: The narrative arc for how partner relationships progress through the PSP lifecycle.

narrativeContexts.context: The PSP journey begins when a PAM is assigned to a partner account, initiating structured discovery through fundamentals worksheets and desk research to understand the partnership rationale and mutual expectations.

Through joint planning workshops and value proposition development, the partnership formalizes expectations with documented revenue targets, SMART initiatives, and sponsorship coverage across the value chain.
Active plan execution drives regular engagement through review cadences, initiative tracking, and performance monitoring, with the PSP serving as the shared roadmap for operational collaboration.
Strategic partnerships sustain value through multi-regional coordination, proactive stakeholder engagement, and annual renewal cycles that deepen the planning discipline with each iteration.

narratives.name: Partner Value Journey
narratives.description: The narrative arc for how partnership value is realized through the PSP methodology.

narrativeContexts.context: Value identification begins with systematic partner business analysis using Ansoff Matrix, capability assessment, and channel model evaluation to understand where mutual value creation opportunities exist.
Value qualification deepens through SWOT comparison and joint brainstorming, producing prioritized opportunity areas that both organizations agree warrant structured initiative investment.

narratives.name: Partner Success Plan Story
narratives.description: The narrative arc for how Partner Success Plans progress through their lifecycle.

narrativeContexts.context: Red Hat and its partners need a structured mechanism to align strategic interests, co-create revenue-generating initiatives, and track mutual value delivery across the partnership lifecycle, replacing ad hoc engagement with disciplined joint planning.

PAMs must develop, validate, and execute comprehensive Partner Success Plans using RHSC, incorporating partnership fundamentals, business analysis, tri-directional value propositions, and rubric-validated quality standards.

The PSP methodology guides PAMs through a structured lifecycle: discovery and analysis, joint planning workshops, initiative definition with GI-SART frameworks, rubric evaluation, and quarterly performance reviews with continuous plan refinement.

Partnerships benefit from measurable revenue growth through jointly planned initiatives, strengthened stakeholder relationships through systematic sponsorship coverage, and continuous improvement through data-driven plan optimization across annual cycles.

narratives.name: Partner Success Planning Journey
narratives.description: The narrative arc for how PAMs develop and sustain partnerships through structured joint planning.

narrativeContexts.context: Partner Account Managers begin the PSP journey by conducting structured partnership discovery — gathering business intelligence through Ansoff Matrix analysis, capability assessment, and SWOT comparison — to understand the partner's strategic direction and identify where Red Hat's technology portfolio intersects with partner growth objectives.

Through facilitated 2.5-hour joint planning workshops, PAMs and partner stakeholders co-create initiatives using GI-SART frameworks and SMART principles, developing tri-directional value propositions and defining revenue targets with base/target/success measures that align both organizations' strategic interests.

Plans move into active execution with configured whitespace maps tracking revenue pipeline, regular review cadences (weekly tactical, monthly status, quarterly executive), and rubric-validated quality assurance ensuring plans consistently meet or exceed the six evaluation criteria across scorecard, alignment, numbers, SMART goals, relationships, and completeness.

Quarterly Business Reviews drive continuous optimization as initiative performance data informs plan adjustments, successful patterns are replicated across segments, and annual renewal cycles incorporate lessons learned — creating a self-reinforcing planning discipline that deepens partnership value over successive cycles.

PAMs and partner stakeholders must co-create initiatives using the GI-SART framework and SMART principles, defining clear financial targets, action plans, and success measures for both revenue and non-revenue goals.

Joint brainstorming sessions identify opportunities, value mapping prioritizes them, and structured frameworks formalize initiatives with base/target/success measures, assigned owners, and tracked action plans in RHSC.

Initiatives deliver measurable outcomes against defined targets, generating proof points for the partnership value proposition and informing next-cycle planning through documented lessons learned and replicated success patterns.

activities.name: Conduct Joint Planning Workshop
activities.description: Prepare, conduct, and follow up on the structured 2.5-hour collaborative planning session with partner stakeholders.

given: Partnership discovery and business analysis are sufficiently advanced to support productive joint planning
Partner stakeholders have agreed to participate and agenda with pre-reads sent 3-5 days in advance

test.name: Workshop execution verification
test.description: Verify that the joint planning workshop produces actionable initiative outcomes.
given: PAM has prepared workshop materials, confirmed stakeholder attendance, and sent pre-reads
when: The 2.5-hour joint planning workshop is executed following the prescribed agenda with majority of time spent listening to partner priorities
then: Workshop produces 1-3 prioritized joint initiatives with SMART goals, assigned owners, and agreed next steps
Draft plan is finalized in RHSC within one week of the workshop

narratives.name: Workshop Facilitation Narrative
narratives.description: How PAMs facilitate productive joint planning workshops.

narrativeContexts.context: Annual planning cycle requires structured joint initiative definition. Partnership discovery and business analysis are complete, providing foundation for productive collaborative planning with partner stakeholders.

Facilitate a 2.5-hour workshop producing 1-3 joint initiatives with SMART goals, following the prescribed agenda allocating 50 minutes to understanding partner priorities before discussing Red Hat strategy.

Execute the timed agenda — Welcome and Context (20 min), Partner and Red Hat Priorities (50 min emphasizing listening), Brainstorm and Narrow (30 min), Draft Plan Elements (20 min), Define Success and Metrics (20 min), Set Actions (10 min) — then consolidate outcomes into RHSC within one week.

Partnership direction is established with prioritized initiatives, assigned ownership, agreed success metrics, and a review cadence, with the PSP finalized in RHSC and internal communications reaching relevant Red Hat teams.

narratives.name: Business Analysis Narrative
narratives.description: How PAMs conduct systematic partner business evaluation.

narrativeContexts.context: A PAM needs to build comprehensive understanding of a partner's business position to inform joint planning and initiative prioritization.

Complete systematic analysis using four structured frameworks — Ansoff Matrix for growth strategy, Capabilities Worksheet for offerings classification, Channel Model for sales alignment, and SWOT for competitive position.

Begin with desk research using public sources and Gemini deep research for Business Model Canvas, then engage partner contacts for collaborative SWOT completion, comparing independent assessments to identify alignment and contrary perceptions.

Analysis insights directly inform initiative brainstorming by revealing growth strategy intersection points, capability gaps addressable through partnership, and prioritized opportunity areas based on mutual benefit.

Complete the tri-directional value proposition with specific What/So What/How Much/Prove It entries for Red Hat to Partner, Partner to Red Hat, and Joint to Customer directions.

Work with partner stakeholders to articulate specific benefits, quantify impact, and identify proof points including customer references and joint project outcomes for each direction, entering completed propositions in RHSC.
Substantiated value propositions are ready for stakeholder communication and customer-facing use, with proof points validated and integrated into GTM materials.

activities.name: Evaluate Plan Quality
activities.description: Score the Partner Success Plan against the six-criterion rubric and generate actionable improvement recommendations.

given: Plan is substantially complete in RHSC with scorecard, initiatives, relationships, and value propositions
Evaluator has rubric criteria understood and access to the evaluation template

test.name: Plan quality evaluation verification
test.description: Verify that rubric-based evaluation produces objective quality assessment.
given: A Partner Success Plan is drafted with all major sections populated in RHSC
when: A manager or PAM applies the six-criterion evaluation rubric, scoring each area on the 0-3 scale
then: Specific improvement areas are identified with actionable feedback
Plan quality level is objectively determined with documented justifications for each score

narratives.name: Plan Quality Evaluation Narrative
narratives.description: How managers and PAMs evaluate plan quality using the rubric.

narrativeContexts.context: Plan quality directly impacts partnership outcomes but varies significantly across PAMs without systematic evaluation and coaching.
Apply the six-criterion rubric (Scorecard, Strategic Alignment, Number Consistency, SMART Goals, Proper Relationships, Completeness) scoring each 0-3 with documented justification.

Systematically evaluate each criterion — verify scorecard completeness, test initiative alignment for win-win-win, check financial consistency, validate SMART compliance, assess relationship coverage, and confirm value chain completeness — documenting specific findings and improvement recommendations.
Plan quality baseline is established with actionable improvement path, informing coaching conversations and driving systematic quality improvement across the team.

citationNames: Rubric for Success Planning CY26

activities.name: Conduct Quarterly Business Review
activities.description: Facilitate periodic reviews of partnership performance against plan targets, adjusting strategies and reinforcing executive engagement.

given: Quarterly cadence milestone is reached and performance data is available in RHSC
Executive sponsors are scheduled to participate

test.name: QBR execution verification
test.description: Verify that quarterly business reviews drive performance improvement.
given: Plan is in active execution with at least one quarter of performance data available
when: QBR is conducted with executive sponsor participation covering initiative performance, relationship health, and strategic alignment
then: Performance gaps are identified with corrective actions and successful patterns are recognized for replication
Plan adjustments are made in RHSC within one week of the QBR

narratives.name: Quarterly Business Review Narrative
narratives.description: How QBRs drive continuous partnership performance improvement.

narrativeContexts.context: QBR preparation involves gathering current performance data from RHSC, updating initiative status and progress fields, and preparing a summary comparing actual results against base/target/success measures.

Execute the review covering achievement highlights, revenue initiative performance (pipeline health, conversion, attainment), non-revenue progress, relationship health, and strategic alignment, with executive sponsor participation.

Assess each initiative against defined measures, perform root cause analysis for underperformance, evaluate non-revenue initiatives for revenue conversion potential, and assess relationship engagement quality.
Update the plan in RHSC with adjustments, communicate outcomes internally, shift resources to reflect performance, document lessons learned, and celebrate wins to reinforce trust and momentum.

activities.name: Review Partnership Relationships
activities.description: Identify, assess, and maintain stakeholder relationships and sponsorship coverage across both organizations and the value chain.

given: Partnership planning requires understanding who is involved on both sides
Partnership fundamentals and business analysis are established

test.name: Relationship review verification
test.description: Verify that stakeholder relationships are comprehensively mapped and gaps addressed.
given: Partnership fundamentals and business analysis are established with planned initiatives
when: PAM completes relationship surveys, sponsorship coverage worksheets, and RHSC relationship maps
then: Every value chain stage has identified sponsors from both organizations with relationship levels assessed
Gaps between current and desired sponsorship coverage are documented with remediation plans

narratives.name: Relationship Review Narrative
narratives.description: How PAMs assess and maintain sponsorship coverage across the value chain.

narrativeContexts.context: Effective plan execution requires sponsorship coverage across the entire value chain from both organizations, but stakeholder landscapes change and relationships require continuous cultivation.
Map stakeholders comprehensively, assess relationship quality at each level (independent, cooperative, partnership), and ensure sponsorship coverage for all six value chain stages.

Identify all relevant contacts, enter them in RHSC relationship maps, complete the Sponsorship Coverage Worksheet, conduct perception-based relationship surveys, determine required relationship level adjustments, and document coverage gaps with implications.
Relationship maps in RHSC visually display all key stakeholders, sponsorship coverage is verified across the value chain, and gaps are being actively addressed through targeted engagement.

test.name: Hierarchy management verification
test.description: Verify that plan hierarchy maintains coherence across organizational levels.
given: Global plan exists and regional/country PAMs need to create aligned subordinate plans
when: Regional PAMs create plans via copy/reparent, customize for regional scope, and align targets with global objectives
then: Regional revenue targets sum to or exceed global targets with clear incrementality documentation
Content at each level addresses prescribed scope sections while connecting to global objectives

narratives.name: Plan Hierarchy Narrative
narratives.description: How GPAMs coordinate plan hierarchy for global partners.

narrativeContexts.context: Global partners require coordinated success plans across multiple regions and countries, with each level contributing to and supporting global objectives while addressing local market conditions.
Establish plan hierarchy using RHSC copy/reparent mechanism, divide content responsibility per scope, and synchronize targets across all levels.

GPAM creates master plan with 5+ global initiatives, regional PAMs copy and customize with region-specific content, country PAMs adapt for local markets, links are documented between plans, and naming conventions are consistently applied.
Coherent plan hierarchy exists where regional targets support global objectives, content is appropriately scoped, and QBR outcomes cascade across levels.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Establish foundation for structured partner planning.

narrativeContexts.context: Foundation is established as PAMs conduct initial partnership discovery, gathering business intelligence through public sources and partner engagement, determining partner type, and beginning plan creation in RHSC with fundamentals documentation.

patternViews.name: Discover and Analyze
patternViews.description: Build comprehensive understanding and strategic alignment.

narrativeContexts.context: Partnership architecture takes shape as systematic business analysis (Ansoff Matrix, SWOT, capabilities) reveals strategic alignment opportunities, joint planning workshops establish shared direction, and candidate initiatives are identified and value-mapped to prioritize mutual benefit.

patternViews.name: Plan and Align
patternViews.description: Co-create initiatives, value propositions, and stakeholder alignment.

narrativeContexts.context: Plan substance is built as initiatives are formalized with GI-SART frameworks and SMART measures, tri-directional value propositions are substantiated with evidence, stakeholder relationships are mapped and assessed, and plan quality is evaluated against the six-criterion rubric before executive approval.

patternViews.name: Execute and Track
patternViews.description: Activate plan with tracking, reviews, and performance monitoring.

narrativeContexts.context: Plan execution operates through established review cadences — weekly tactical, monthly status, and quarterly executive reviews — with initiative performance tracked against measures, whitespace maps reflecting pipeline health, and executive sponsors maintaining strategic engagement as the partnership delivers against its targets.

patternViews.name: Optimize and Renew
patternViews.description: Refine through performance insights and prepare next cycle.

narrativeContexts.context: Performance data drives continuous optimization as QBRs inform plan adjustments, successful initiative patterns are replicated across segments, non-revenue achievements convert to revenue opportunities, and annual renewal creates a fresh plan incorporating all accumulated learnings for the next planning cycle.
